info.description:
Multi-vendor commerce OMS API.

**Conventions**
- Base path `/api/v1`. Breaking changes ship as `/api/v2`; additive changes stay in v1.
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`. Tenant is derived from the token, never from the request body.
- Success: `{ "success": true, "data": ..., "requestId": "..." }`. Lists add `meta: { limit, nextCursor, hasMore }`.
- Errors: `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message", "details" }, "requestId": "..." }`.
- Pagination: keyset (`?limit=25&cursor=...`). Sorting: `?sort=-createdAt,name`. Filtering: `?filter[status]=active`. Search: `?q=`.
- Retriable POSTs accept `Idempotency-Key` (required where documented).
- Every response carries `X-Request-Id` and `X-Correlation-Id`.

post.summary: Create a stock transfer between warehouses (draft)

patch.description: Only a draft can be edited (409 INVALID_STATE otherwise). Send any of the warehouses, the whole `items` list (it replaces the old one) and `notes` (null clears them). Editing never moves stock: it moves only when the draft is submitted. `version` is optional optimistic concurrency (409 `stale_draft` when someone else changed the draft first).

post.summary: Submit a draft transfer: the stock moves now
post.description: The only step that moves stock for a draft. In one transaction (all or nothing) the stock leaves the source warehouse and is received by the destination, so the ledger shows transfer_out + incoming + receive. 409 INSUFFICIENT_STOCK (with `details.shortages`) when the source cannot cover a line; nothing changes then. Idempotent: submitting a transfer that is already received changes nothing and answers `duplicate: true`; a cancelled transfer is refused (409). Discard a draft with POST /inventory/transfers/{id}/cancel instead.

duplicate.description: true when the transfer was already submitted (nothing changed)

post.summary: Ship a transfer
post.description: Stock leaves the source warehouse now and shows as `incoming` at the destination.

post.summary: Receive a transfer
post.description: Defaults to receiving everything that was shipped. Pass `items` for a partial receipt: the shortfall is written back to the source warehouse.

post.summary: Cancel a transfer
post.description: A draft is simply cancelled; an in-transit transfer returns the stock to the source warehouse.

post.summary: Announce an inbound shipment (expected goods)

post.summary: Receive goods (good + damaged), optionally into a bin
post.description: `receivedQuantity` is what physically arrived now; `damagedQuantity` is the damaged part of it (goes to the damaged bucket, not sellable). Partial receipts are fine; the shipment becomes `received` when every line is complete. Over-receipts are accepted and reported in `overReceived`.

post.summary: Close a part-received shipment (clears what will never arrive)

post.summary: Preview an adjustment (nothing is written)
post.description: Runs the real adjustment inside a rolled-back savepoint: it fails with exactly the errors the write would (never negative, never below reserved) and otherwise returns `currentAvailable`, `adjustment`, `newAvailable` and warnings for that location.

post.summary: Adjust stock by type (damage / return / correction / manual / shrinkage / other)
post.description: One ledger movement in the audit trail. `damage` moves available -> damaged (direction `increase` restores); `return` records a customer return (held in the returned bucket unless `disposition: restock`); `shrinkage` writes off lost units as its own movement type (a loss: `quantity` units leave on-hand, `direction` may only be `decrease`); `correction` / `manual` / `other` change on-hand by `quantity` in `direction`, or `correction` can pass a physical count `setOnHand`. `other` requires a `note`.

post.summary: Bulk action on a selection (adjust / transfer / export / sync / group)
post.description: `selection.mode = ids` takes at most 500 variants; `all_matching` takes the ledger filters and processes up to 5000 variants (413 beyond: narrow the filters). Every variant is its own unit of work (its own savepoint), so one failure never blocks the others: the response lists `{ variantId, ok, error? }` per variant. `adjust`: params = adjustment fields (+ optional warehouseId, default = the location holding most stock); `transfer`: fromWarehouseId, toWarehouseId, quantity (creates ONE draft transfer for the variants that have enough stock); `export`: returns the CSV inline; `sync`: queues an inventory sync for every channel account the selection is listed on; `group`: groupId or groupName (created if missing).

Valuation = on-hand units x variant cost price (variants without a cost are counted in `skusWithoutCost`, never guessed). Channel freshness comes from the last successful inventory sync job.

The "Recent stock movements" list: SKU, product, warehouse, readable type, signed quantity, resulting available, reference (order / transfer number), reason and operator name. Keyset paging: pass `meta.nextCursor` as `cursor`. The raw ledger stays at GET /inventory/movements.

post.description: Runs the three steps of the listing flow and reports each one. 202 when the publish job was queued; 200 when it stopped earlier (`outcome` blocked: validation errors, failed: a step was refused, not_applicable: already live) with the step that stopped it. post.summary: Publish many listings (validate, approve, publish each)
post.description: At most 100 ids. Always HTTP 200: every listing has its own result (`done` with the job id, `failed` with the reason, `skipped` when already live); one failure never stops the rest.

post.summary: Bulk action on listings: validate | publish | unpublish | retry | sync_inventory
post.description: At most 100 ids, partial success inside HTTP 200 (per-item `status` done | skipped | failed). retry: rejected / correction-required listings go through the publish flow again, a failed content update is re-sent, a pending listing is re-checked. sync_inventory flags the active listings and queues one stock job per account.

get.description: Computed from the stored readiness of every listing (no marketplace call). overall.readinessPct = listings that can still be published and have no blocking check / all of them (null: none to publish). spectrum counts listings by state (ready = live, ready to publish or syncing; needs_review; blocked = blocking errors or rejected) plus the not-listed candidates. health scores each readiness group (pass 1, warn 0.5, fail 0) and, computed from the master catalogue, Variants (options set, SKU, barcode, price, an image per variant, every variant listed on the account) and Compliance (HSN code, GST rate, country of origin, manufacturer or brand, weight, MRP present, price within MRP, category attributes once validated); each check scores the share of variants or listings that pass it. Order: content, attributes, media, variants, compliance, then price, stock, category, marketplace. coverage = active products with a live listing per connected marketplace. journey = the steps of one sample listing that needs attention. suggestions = missing category attributes, with a value the same product already has elsewhere (apply with PATCH /listings/{id} attributeOverrides).

get.summary: Publishing preparation: the ready catalogue cohort and its potential issues
get.description: Cohort = listings that can still go through the publish flow (draft, ready, approved, rejected, correction required). A listing is ready when its stored readiness has no blocking check. issues list every blocking and warning check (blockers first, at most 100; issuesTotal is the full count). readyListingIds (at most 500) feed POST /listings/bulk-publish, 100 per call. channels carry the pricing rule (active pricing policy) and the sync mode (webhooks / polling interval from the connector) of each channel; publishLock states what the approval locks. Nothing is published by this read.

Other channels of the product: GET /listings/{id}/channels. Poll while state = syncing.

Always HTTP 200 with a result per listing (`done`, `skipped` when nothing changes, `failed` with the reason, e.g. VERSION_CONFLICT when `versions` is sent and the listing changed). Listings of one product on one marketplace share their content, so the edit is applied once for them. `dryRun` returns the before / after without saving.

get.description: Whether the connector is verified against the real marketplace (`live`) or only runs against its sandbox, and the mode a new connection gets by default.

get.summary: Connector directory merged with my accounts
get.description: Every connector with its setup form (`authFlow`) and its state for this seller: `connected` (at least one healthy account), `needs_attention` (an account is unhealthy or not finished), `available`, or `unavailable` (planned, or switched off for this business). Ratings, reviews and prices are always null: the platform does not collect them.

One card per marketplace account with live numbers: active listings, pending orders, sync state and progress, last and next sync, token expiry, a 0-100 health score (40% connection state, 40% sync success of the last 24 h, 20% token health), friction points and the capability list.

get.summary: One account for the detail page
get.description: The card plus the capability matrix, readiness notes, the last sync jobs, per-lane success of the last 24 hours, webhook status, the inventory policy and the listing counts by status.

get.summary: Connection health of the whole network
get.description: Overall pulse (average account health score), per-lane success rate and throughput from the sync jobs of the last 24 hours (network wide and per account), totals, one row per account, the tokens that are expiring or expired, and what the connections that need attention put at risk (stale stock, rejected listings, open orders).

post.summary: Sync an account now
post.description: Queues the sync jobs for the requested scopes (orders, inventory, listings = listing status checks, catalog = product import); default is everything the connector supports. Scopes the connector cannot do are reported in `skipped`. A queued job of the same kind is reused (`created: false`). Poll GET .../sync-status for progress.

created.description: false = an equivalent queued job was reused

get.summary: Combined sync progress of an account
get.description: Percent done across the running jobs, the running jobs, and the latest job of each type from the last 24 hours.

latest.description: The most recent job of every type in the last 24 hours

post.summary: Connect a marketplace in one call
post.description: Creates the account, authorizes it, tests the connection and queues the first sync, reporting every step (`steps[{name, ok, message, durationMs}]`). Send `credentials` (the form from the directory `authFlow.fields`), or for redirect connectors send no credentials with `redirectUri` to get the URL to send the seller to, then finish with `code` + `state` (or POST /marketplace-hub/oauth/complete). A failed attempt removes the account it created. Requires a verified e-mail address (403 EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED). The Idempotency-Key header makes a retry return the first result.

mode.description: Default: live when the connector is verified for live use, otherwise sandbox

credentials.description: The form from the connector authFlow.fields (secrets are sent once, stored encrypted, never returned)

config.description: Non-secret account configuration, e.g. the Shopify shopDomain for the redirect flow

code.description: Authorization code returned after the redirect (needs `state`; the account is the one the state was issued for)

externalAccountId.description: Seller id returned next to the code by marketplaces that send it separately (e.g. Amazon selling_partner_id)

redirectUri.description: Where the marketplace sends the seller back; required to START a redirect connection

post.summary: Finish a redirect connection
post.description: Call this from the page the marketplace redirects the seller back to, with the `state` and `code` of the redirect. The pending account is found from the signed state (10 minutes, bound to this business). Same steps and result as POST /marketplace-hub/connect.

get.summary: Where to send the seller to (re)authorize an account
get.description: For redirect connectors: the marketplace URL plus a signed 10-minute `state` bound to this account (CSRF protection). Use it to reconnect an expired account; to start a new connection use POST /marketplace-hub/connect.

get.summary: The editing page of a product in one call
get.description: The editor view of the product, the baseline `version` to send with the save, the master-code lock (`locks.productCode`), header meta (master code, created, last updated and by whom), the nav with counts, the attribute counter (supplied core facts + confirmed custom attributes) with its note, media thumbnails, the channels that inherit the master content (and the fields each manages independently), the readiness panel (`readiness.percent` equals the content readiness of GET /products/{id}/content) and the suggested improvements. Writes nothing.

post.summary: What would this edit affect? (preview, nothing is saved)
post.description: Compares `changes` with the stored product (values equal to it are ignored) and answers which connected listings would inherit each change, which channels manage that content independently, and whether the seller must confirm (a category or product-type change while listings are live: `requiresConfirmation`, with the modal text in `confirmation`). `errors` lists fields that the save would reject; they are left out of the impact. Updates are not sent to listings until the product is saved.

post.summary: Save the edit page (atomic) and propagate to the connected listings
post.description: ONE transaction: the product is patched with the strict field rules of the creation flow, the connected listings are marked (inherited content -> `sync_pending`, a category change on live listings -> `needs_review`, no `listings.update` capability -> `needs_republish`, channel overrides are never touched), then audit `product.edited` and the events `product.updated` / `product.edited` are written. After the commit one content-sync job per account is requested. Errors: 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` (`details.issues[{ path, code, message }]`), 409 `VERSION_CONFLICT` (`details.currentVersion`, `current` editor view, `updatedAt`, `updatedBy`), 409 `CONFLICT` with `details.rule` = `code_locked` (the master code of a non-draft), `confirmation_required` (with `details.impact`; repeat with `confirm: true`) or `needs_variant`, 413 when the product has more than 500 listings. A save without an effective change answers 200 `{ saved: false, noChanges: true }` and writes nothing. Honours the Idempotency-Key header.

get.description: Every suggestion that currently applies and is not dismissed (`items`), and those the seller dismissed that still apply (`dismissed`, to offer a restore). Keys: `description_short` (the plain-text description is shorter than the median of the business's other active products in the same category, at least 5 of them, else 150 characters) and `few_images` (fewer than 3 real images; a placeholder does not count). A suggestion whose condition no longer holds disappears on its own.

post.summary: Dismiss a suggested improvement
post.description: Per product and key. With `until` the suggestion may reappear after that moment (must be in the future); without it, it stays hidden until restored. Idempotent: dismissing again updates the dismissal. 404 for an unknown key.

post.summary: Show a dismissed suggestion again
post.description: Removes the dismissal. Idempotent. 404 for an unknown key.
